Hi CJ — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Recap from today
- PulseHealth is primarily concerned with admin activity and API request logs (who did what, when, and from where) for incident investigation and regulatory audits.
- You mentioned a 7-year retention baseline for certain records, and the need to demonstrate exportability and immutability for selected datasets.
- Primary compliance drivers: HIPAA (PHI handling) and internal financial controls.

2) Info we promised to share
- Redwood security overview + SOC 2 status (attached).
- High-level export formats we support (CSV / NDJSON) and sample column sets.
- Proposed playbook for exporting admin activity and API logs, and options for write-once storage.

3) Questions for your team (please reply inline)
- Which exact event types do you need exported as part of a standard evidence package (admin actions, user auth events, API calls, system events)?
- Do you require cryptographic signing of exported artifacts, or is WORM object storage sufficient?
- Any preferred transfer mechanism (S3 pull, S3 push, scp, signed download link)?

Next steps
- If you can share your vendor questionnaire (or highlight must-have fields), Marissa will map answers to it and circulate a technical appendix.
- Suggest a 30-min technical deep-dive next week with Rishi to walk through sample exports and retention policies.

I attached a short security overview and a one-page export spec to start — Marissa will follow up with the vendor questionnaire mapping.

Thanks,

Thanks, Sergio — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Event types: we definitely need admin actions (role changes, grant/revoke, admin console changes), API request logs tied to request IDs, authentication events (including MFA challenges), and data-access events where PHI could be involved.
- Retention/immutability: our baseline is 7 years, but for incident forensics we may ask for snapshots that are immutable for a rolling 12–24 month period. For long-term retention we accept immutable copies stored in a customer-managed S3 with WORM policies.
- Evidence transfer: prefer S3 push integrations (server-to-server) where Redwood writes a timestamped snapshot to our S3. If needed, signed URLs are okay for ad-hoc pulls.

I attached our vendor questionnaire (PulseHealth_Vendor_Q.pdf) — not everything on there is a blocker but please flag any items you can't support.

Let's get the technical deep-dive on the calendar. Rishi is the right person to engage with on export formats and immutability.

—CJ

Hi CJ / Sergio — following up with concrete answers and attachments (see below). I answered inline in the vendor questionnaire PDF and included a short technical appendix. Highlights: 

- Event types: Redwood can produce time-ordered event exports for: admin console actions (role changes, key rotations), API request traces (request_id, caller, endpoint, payload hashes), authentication events (login attempt, success/failure, MFA), and data-access events (record-level access logs where available).

- Export formats & delivery: supported formats are NDJSON (recommended for streams), compressed CSV (for table-like ingestion), and Parquet for analytics. Delivery options: 
  * S3 push (Redwood will write to customer bucket with timestamped prefixes and object manifests)
  * S3 presigned PUT if customer prefers control
  * Signed HTTPS download for ad-hoc evidence pulls

- Immutability & verification: for short-term immutable snapshots we support writing to object storage with server-side WORM-compatible policies (object-lock) and SHA256 manifests for file integrity. For stronger cryptographic evidence, we can sign manifests with a Redwood key and provide verification instructions.

- Retention windows: configurable per-workload; default hosted retention is 90 days for high-volume logs but customer-managed S3 allows you to retain as long as required. For your 7-year requirement we recommend a daily export/archival job to your S3 with lifecycle policies.

- SOC 2 & evidence: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant (report available under NDA). I included a link in the questionnaire PDF for our compliance artifacts and an exported sample of admin events (Audit_Exports_Specs.csv).

Next steps proposed: 
- Rishi: can you prepare a 10–15 row NDJSON sample (including request_id and hash manifest) and a short write-up on our object-lock recommendation? Target: Wed 07 Apr.
- CJ / PulseHealth: confirm preferred S3 transfer mode and provide a test bucket ARN or let us know if you want Redwood to initiate a presigned upload flow.
- Sergio: I can run the vendor question mapping and return a single .pdf with callouts.

Thanks — attaching: vendor-question-response.pdf, sample-export-ndjson.ndjson (redacted), and the SOC 2 evidence request link.

Best,
